newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday on profit-taking after the market's four consecutive record closes.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 33.87 points at 6,728.42, retreating from Tuesday's high of 6,762.29. In late morning, the index lost more than 50 points, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to activate its curbs on programme trading.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-10 on active volume of 293 million shares on the NYSE.

Analysts said the market also was disappoined that the stock of Intel Corp. did not take flight after the company reported late on Tuesday very strong earnings. Intel, whose earnings more than doubled in the fourth quarter, was off 1-5/8 at 145-1/2.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is heavily weighted with high technology stocks, was down 5.54 points at 1340.82. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.90 at 585.45.

The bond market, which jumped a full point on Tuesday, was also under selling pressure. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost half a point, raising its yield to 6.81 percent from 6.77 percent at Tuesday's close.

"Bonds had a good day yesterday and that gave rise to a rally in the stock market," said George Pirrone, senior trader at Dreyfus Corp. "Today, bonds are down and Intel is not shining the way people hoped it would this morning."
"This is a very volatile market. We are beginning to look a little worn out in the (stock) averages," he said.
The drop in technology stocks was due to the fact that the sector had a strong run prior to the announcement of Intel's results, analysts said.
Among high technology stocks, International Business Machines Corp., was down 1/4 at 166-5/8 and Microsoft Corp. lost 1/8 to 85-1/4.

"The high techs are used as a trading vehicle," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities. "When the economy looks like it's growing they are bought, and when it comes time to take profits they are the first to be sold out of a portfolio."
She said that investors were in a mood to take profits.
"There is a sentiment that things are so good that they can't possibly get any better. Where do we go from here? Might as well take profits," Farley said.

Among special situations, Tencor Instruments rose 6-5/8 to 37-1/8 after the company announced late Tuesday that it agreed to be acquired by KLA Instruments Corp. in a one-for-one stock swap. KLA was down 1/2 at 40-3/8.
